name: Fort Worth
tagline: Cowtown Culture, No State Income Tax, and Genuine Texas Affordability
description: Fort Worth delivers authentic Texas culture with significantly more affordability than its neighbor Dallas. The Stockyards, world-class museums along the Cultural District, and a revitalized downtown with craft breweries and live music make it far more than a cowboy town. With zero state income tax and housing costs well below the national average, Fort Worth is one of the most practical FIRE destinations in America for those who want big-city amenities without the big-city price tag.

quickFacts.visa: No visa required for US citizens
quickFacts.climate: Subtropical with hot summers and mild winters

housing.description: Cheapest acceptable older studio or 1BR in a workable area — Fairmount, Arlington Heights, or the Ridgmar/Western Hills edge

dining.description: Mostly home cooking; BBQ, Tex-Mex, and casual diners a couple of times a week

healthcare.description: A subsidized ACA marketplace Silver plan, assuming annual income stays under the 2026 subsidy cutoff of about $62,600 for a single person; Texas did not expand Medicaid and offers no state subsidy above that line, so the full price runs about $900 a month. Priced for an early retiree aged 45-55; older retirees should budget more.

transportation.description: A paid-off used car with insurance and gas — essential for getting around (Texas auto insurance runs above the US average)

entertainment.description: Free Stockyards cattle drives, Trinity River trails, and the Kimbell's permanent collection

1M.lifestyle: A cheapest-acceptable older studio or one-bedroom in Fairmount, Arlington Heights, or the Ridgmar edge, cooking at home most nights with BBQ or Tex-Mex out a couple of times a week. The Stockyards cattle drives and the Kimbell's permanent collection are free. No state income tax helps, though summer A/C bills are a meaningful expense — utilities are Fort Worth's one above-average line. The ACA Silver premium stays low only if MAGI is kept under the 2026 ~$62,600 cliff (Texas has no backfill). A manageable Lean budget with genuine big-city amenities.

housing.description: A decent typical 1BR in a solid neighborhood — the Cultural District, Arlington Heights, or Ridglea

dining.description: Regular dining along Magnolia Avenue, at Stockyards steakhouses, and in Sundance Square

healthcare.description: A Silver plan; net cost low only if MAGI is managed under the ~$62,600 cliff (no Texas backfill)

transportation.description: A reliable truck or SUV with full coverage

entertainment.description: TCU football, rodeo tickets, Kimbell and Modern memberships, live music at Billy Bob's

2M.lifestyle: A decent one-bedroom in the Cultural District, Arlington Heights, or Ridglea, regular dining along Magnolia Avenue and at Stockyards steakhouses, and TCU football tickets. A reliable truck or SUV with full coverage is covered, along with weekend drives to the Hill Country or trips to Big Bend. No state income tax and moderate housing costs leave a healthy monthly margin — a comfortable, culturally full life.

housing.description: A high-quality 1BR in a walkable district — West 7th / Crockett Row, downtown, or the Rivercrest edge

dining.description: Frequent fine dining at Grace, Clay Pigeon, and Lonesome Dove

healthcare.description: A Gold-tier plan; padded near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff where premium tax credits disappear

transportation.description: A late-model truck or luxury SUV, premium insurance, occasional rideshare

entertainment.description: Colonial Country Club events, premium TCU and Rangers tickets, rodeo VIP, art collecting

3M.lifestyle: A high-quality place in a walkable district like West 7th or near Rivercrest, regular dinners at Grace and Lonesome Dove, and premium TCU and Rangers tickets. A late-model truck or luxury SUV handles daily life, and healthcare is a padded Gold plan near the ~$62,600 ACA cliff. This is a genuinely affluent life by Fort Worth standards, with no state income tax and affordable housing leaving substantial room for travel and saving.

dining.description: Near-daily fine dining plus a private chef for ranch-style entertaining

healthcare.description: An unsubsidized Gold/Platinum plan plus concierge medicine through Baylor Scott & White or Texas Health

transportation.description: A luxury truck and sedan, premium insurance, detailing

entertainment.description: A country club membership (Colonial, Shady Oaks), premium Cowboys and Rangers tickets, cultural patronage

5M.lifestyle: A luxury West 7th high-rise or a Clearfork rental, cleaning a couple of times a week, and a country club membership at Colonial or Shady Oaks. Near-daily fine dining, a nice truck and sedan, and business-class travel are all within budget, with weekend ranch getaways and concierge care through Baylor Scott & White. No state income tax makes every withdrawal go further — a well-staffed, comfortable life.

dining.description: Private-chef dining, catered events, and ranch gatherings

healthcare.description: A top-tier unsubsidized plan plus concierge medicine and executive wellness

transportation.description: A premium truck or SUV with full ownership costs, plus regular private car service

entertainment.description: Premium club-level Cowboys season tickets, major philanthropic events, Western art collecting, international travel

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeping several days a week plus grounds and property upkeep

luxuryExtras.description: A working ranch operation, first-class international travel, major art acquisitions, charitable foundations

10M.lifestyle: A historic Rivercrest estate or a ranch property outside the city, household help several days a week, and occasional private-chef evenings alongside the city's best steakhouses and dining rooms. First-class travel, premium club-level Cowboys season tickets, and concierge healthcare are all covered. No state income tax and Fort Worth's moderate cost base mean this budget — roughly $199k a year — delivers very comfortable, low-friction living with large margins.
